comparison_A2_5.computed_by: src/exposure_schema.py (the validator), not by this session's own count — A2.5
comparison_A2_5.verdict: ARCHITECTURE.md's central claim does NOT survive in the form stated.
comparison_A2_5.finding:
A2.1 registered that this block could falsify the document that commissioned it, and it does.

THE ACCIDENT CLASS DOES NOT COMPLETE BETTER. On the field rate — the measure with any n behind it — accidents are LOWER: 28.6% of required fields filled against the attack class's 37.3%. On COMPLETE rate accidents are nominally higher, 14.3% against 6.7%, but that is one event out of seven and no weight can rest on it.

PER FIELD, THE ONLY ADVANTAGE IS THE ASSET'S STANDING PROPERTY. capacity_nameplate_kbd runs 26.7% for attacks against 42.9% for accidents — the one field where the reporting regime plainly differs, because US refinery nameplate capacity is a statutory annual EIA publication. Every field that describes THE OUTAGE is the same or worse: capacity_affected 17.3% vs 14.3%, days_to_partial 22.7% vs 14.3%, days_to_full 20.0% vs 14.3%.

AND THE TARGET N WAS NOT REACHABLE. Joe set 40-60 on the premise that EIA published weekly capacity offline and confirmed restoration through Katrina, Rita, Ike, Harvey and Ida. Eight routes were tested (see routes_not_yielding) and every one returns REGIONAL AGGREGATE or is gone: EIA's own 2005 daily hurricane reports no longer resolve, DOE's situation reports count refineries without naming or sizing them, ISER's refinery-disruption register refuses connection, and web.archive.org cannot be fetched. Under A2.2 the shortfall is itself the measurement: the premise that this data is readily available is not supported.

WHAT SURVIVES OF THE FIVE REASONS. 'Category mismatch' survives and is strengthened — hurricanes fail asset identification 0 of 4 here, exactly as campaign-type attacks did in block A, so the mismatch belongs to the schema and the event's geometry rather than to conflict. 'Closed archives' survives but is NOT specific to conflict: the closed archive here is the US federal government's own. What does NOT survive is any claim resting on belligerent behaviour — contested fields, incompatible units, forecast-not-confirmed restoration. Those cannot explain missing durations in a class with no belligerent in it, and the durations are missing there at the same rate.

THE HONEST STATEMENT THE DATA SUPPORTS: restoration data is not published at event level for anyone. The 6% figure is real but it is not a measurement of conflict opacity; it is a measurement of the fact that no reporting regime, statutory or otherwise, records how much capacity a specific incident removed and when it came back. The one row that completes does so because the refinery never reopened, which makes both duration fields determinate by ending the question rather than answering it.
comparison_A2_5.limitation_restated: Amendment 1 §A1.4 registered it before any number: the accident set is US assets under EIA and CSB mandates and the attack set is not, so any gap is cause confounded with reporting regime. With n=7 the accident side cannot carry a rate comparison on its own, and the field-rate comparison is the one with support.
